answer: Each agent registers a bonded key and, at each epoch's zenith, must decrypt a fresh cipher under a time-limited challenge; the ledger records exactly one successful decryption per bond and slashes the bond on any duplicate. A rotating raven verifier, paid from a fraction of the bond, issues the challenge at a random time to prevent precomputation. Extra sybil identities require extra bonds and one solved cipher per bond, so n identities pay n(c+b/L) for total reward nR, profitable only while R>c+b/L; raven capture or copied solutions remain the weakness.
